🤖 **Agent note** · triage verdict (queue task 12814, lane bf419306-c4ef-470f-a553-beabf93239de, 2026-11-08)

## Verdict: REAL AND CURRENT — design remainder confirmed, converted to a work packet

Worked directly by the opencode claimant this time (the previous lanes handed task 12814 off without binding; this lane is the claimant and drives it to a terminal state).

Re-verified fresh at `origin/main` `cc09dd4f5f`:

- Issue #5837 is OPEN with `task/triage`, `app/id`, `status/triaged` — no hard-stop labels (`held`, `user/owned`, `do-not-merge`, `do-not-auto-edit`).
- **No PR and no branch implements it.** `gh pr list --search 5837` returns only unrelated matches (#3375, #135 merged; #7792 is the *Obsidian importer* design for #5845, a different cluster). No `doc/` record covers the graph view.
- **Not implemented:** `grep -ril "graph_view|graphview" pkgs/id --include=*.rs` returns nothing.
- **Not a duplicate of a landed sibling.** #5848 (Joplin importer, CLOSED) explicitly puts the graph view out of scope: *"cluster features, other importers, the graph view — is out of scope"* (`doc/2026-11-08_design_id5848.md` §7). The graph-view cluster is genuinely unsettled.
- Parent #5678 is OPEN and currently `status/blocked`; its blocker is a *parent-level* packet defect (task 12248: the parent tracker has no remaining parent-level acceptance beyond its filed children), which does **not** invalidate this child. Programme epic #2056 OPEN.

## Why this is not the parent's defect repeating

Task 12248 blocked the parent because a generic parent-level small_fix would compete with the already-filed child designs. This ticket is one of those children, and it has a concrete, self-contained deliverable that no other issue carries — so converting it to a packet is the correct routing, not a competing fix.

## Remaining scope

| Facet | Settle |
| --- | --- |
| Local vs global graph | What the graph shows by default — the neighbourhood of the current note, or the whole vault — and how a user moves between the two |
| Edge types | Which relations render as edges: typed references (links), backlinks, tag claims, and typed relations from the #2048 object model; how each is visually distinguished |
| Filtering | Filter dimensions (note type, tag, collection, link type, time) and whether filters compose |
| Performance on large vaults | The scale target, the query path over the triple/index layer, and what degrades first — with a stated budget rather than "fast" |
| Multiplayer / live graph | How concurrent edits and live revisions appear in an open graph; whether the graph is eventually consistent and what the user sees meanwhile |

## Ordering / blockers

- The object model is fixed by [#2048](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/2048) (`doc/2026-11-01_design_id2048.md`, PR #3885) — stable note IDs, signed revisions, structured typed references, tags as observed-remove claims. This design **consumes** those decisions and must not re-decide them.
- The query substrate is the parent's triple/ANSI SQL-PGQ direction (#5688 family); the performance facet should state its target against that layer rather than inventing a separate index.
- Siblings that feed it: #5843 (extensibility) and #5839 (content model) may constrain what a node is; neither is a hard gate for recording the view design, and any constraint taken from them must be cited with its issue number.
- Where this design would change a parent #5678 decision, record it explicitly on the parent rather than forking silently.

## Routing

Converted to a work packet (dedupe `repo-health:v1:fix:developing-today/code:issue:5837`) scoped to that decision record. Per Drew's triage doctrine this triage does **not** close the issue — the issue returns to the queue for the real design work.
